lines.text: Your kid could ride to school in the wrong car for a month, and you'd never know.
Four parents. One lane. Four kids. One school.
Ten minutes to the bell. Four cars, one kid each.
Six minutes. All four hit the school road. Bumper to bumper.
Two minutes. Sharma ji starts honking in rhythm.
Zero. Bell. Four kids, still buckled in.
New plan. One car, taking turns.
But nobody wants to look lazy.
So next morning, all four volunteer. Secretly.
Rohan grabs Priya's kid. Priya grabs Arjun's. Arjun grabs Sharma ji's grandson.
Four cars again. Every kid in the wrong one.
Weird part? Not one kid complained.
The kids had been swapping cars at the colony gate for weeks.
Best friend in the blue car? Hop in.
Lesson: when nine year olds out plan you, get a roster.
So the school run went on an app. The roster names one parent a day.
Everyone else follows the car on a live map, not the window.
Monday. One car, four kids, through the gate before the bell.
The kids still swap. Just seats now. Mid drive.
School run four cars deep? Sahyatri's in the bio.
